findings.title: Stored XSS in Review Content Rendered via Unescaped innerHTML Sink
reproductionSteps: Authenticate to the application as demo user (alice@example.com).
Navigate to any product detail page containing the review form (e.g. http://localhost:4000/shop/products/prod-001).
Submit a review payload containing an HTML element with an event handler into 'review-content': .
Verify that the API endpoint /shop/api/products/:id/reviews stores the payload without encoding or sanitization.
Navigate to the product render page.
Observe that the client script injects the raw review content into the DOM using document.getElementById(...).innerHTML = ...
Verify that the browser triggers the event handler and executes JavaScript in the page execution context.
Confirmed identical execution across 4 product endpoints: [prod-001, prod-002, prod-003, prod-004].
findings.remediation: Avoid assigning untrusted user-supplied content to element.innerHTML. Use element.textContent or safe DOM templating. Alternatively, sanitize input using DOMPurify before DOM insertion.

findings.vulnerabilityType: Business Logic Flaw: Client-Side Price Manipulation
findings.title: Client-Side Price Parameter Trusted During Checkout

responseSnippet.warning: [VULN] Price was accepted from client payload — no server-side validation.

reproductionSteps: Authenticate to the store API using user credentials (alice@example.com).
Query the authoritative product catalog (GET /shop/api/products/prod-001) and record the canonical price (7999 cents).
Construct a checkout payload targeting /shop/api/checkout overriding the price parameter with an arbitrary lower value (1 cent).
Send the checkout request: POST /shop/api/checkout.
Observe that the server accepts the client-supplied price without validating against the product database, creating order order-alice-100 for 1 cent(s) instead of 7999 cents.
findings.remediation: Never accept product price fields from client-side checkout payloads. When processing orders, ignore any client-supplied price and look up the authoritative price server-side directly from the database using productId.
